issues.legal_issue: The urgency power to dispense with the objection inquiry does not extend to land outside the categories covered by the original possession provision merely because the acquisition falls within a locally expanded urgency category.
material_facts: The land was not waste or arable, and that fact was not disputed.
The government used the urgency provision to dispense with the statutory objection inquiry for an acquisition treated as falling within the locally expanded category for taking possession.
issues.conclusion: The direction dispensing with the objection inquiry was invalid. Because the required inquiry had not been held, the subsequent acquisition declaration was also invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5-A and 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, the inquiry may be dispensed with only for land to which Section 17(1) or Section 17(2) applies. The Uttar Pradesh amendment adding Section 17(1-A) extended the power to take possession before an award in specified circumstances, but did not extend the separate power under Section 17(4) to dispense with the inquiry. The Court applied Nandeshwar Prasad v. U.P. Government. A declaration under Section 6 made without the obligatory Section 5-A procedure is invalid.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and land_is_not_waste_or_arable and acquisition_falls_within_locally_expanded_urgency_category and objection_inquiry_is_dispensed_with

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated compulsory acquisition proceedings for land.
predicates.land_is_not_waste_or_arable: The land being acquired was not waste or arable land.
predicates.acquisition_falls_within_locally_expande: The acquisition fell within a locally expanded category that permitted possession before an award.
predicates.objection_inquiry_is_dispensed_with: The government directed that interested persons would not receive the statutory inquiry into objections.

issues.definition: When acquisition proceedings concern land outside the waste-or-arable category, falling within a locally expanded urgency category does not make a direction dispensing with the objection inquiry valid.

issues.legal_issue: An urgency direction dispensing with the objection inquiry cannot be upheld for only the qualifying portion when the acquisition also covers land outside the qualifying categories.
material_facts: The acquisition notification covered land of which, at most, only part was said to be waste or arable.
The direction dispensing with the inquiry applied to the notified land, and interested persons could not be restricted to objecting only about the non-waste-or-arable portion.
issues.conclusion: The direction dispensing with the inquiry was invalid for the notified land as a whole and could not be treated as partly valid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5-A and 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, where the government lacks power to dispense with the inquiry for any part of the notified land, the notification cannot be severed so as to dispense with the inquiry for another part. Interested persons must be able to raise objections concerning the notified land as a whole.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated compulsory acquisition proceedings for land.
predicates.acquisition_notification_covers_mixed_la: The notified land included both land within and land outside the categories for which the inquiry could be dispensed with.
predicates.inquiry_exemption_covers_the_entire_noti: The government purported to dispense with the objection inquiry for all land covered by the notification.

issues.definition: If an acquisition notification covers land in mixed categories and the inquiry exemption applies to all of it, the exemption is invalid for the whole notified area.

issues.legal_issue: The record did not establish that abandonment of an earlier acquisition proceeding barred a fresh proceeding for the same land.
material_facts: An earlier acquisition proceeding had been abandoned, and a fresh proceeding was later started for some of the same land.
The earlier officer’s report was not before the Court, and the record did not establish that the government had accepted that report as the reason for abandoning the earlier proceeding.
The later proceeding covered a smaller area than the earlier one.
issues.conclusion: The Court could not hold on the available evidence that the government was prohibited from commencing a fresh acquisition proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: The Court did not decide the merits of whether a prior decision on objections could bar fresh acquisition proceedings. It held that such a conclusion could not be reached without evidence showing the contents and acceptance of the earlier report and what had led the government to abandon the earlier proceeding.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated compulsory acquisition proceedings for land.
predicates.fresh_proceeding_follows_abandoned_proce: The government began a fresh acquisition proceeding after abandoning an earlier proceeding concerning the land.
predicates.record_does_not_show_prior_report_was_ac: The court record does not establish that the government accepted the earlier officer’s report or what prompted abandonment.

issues.definition: When a fresh acquisition follows abandonment but the record does not establish why the earlier proceeding was abandoned or whether its report was accepted, a bar on fresh acquisition is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A ground not raised before the High Court, or not pursued there, need not be considered for the first time in an appeal from its decision on a writ petition.
material_facts: The objection that the land was not sufficiently specified had not been raised before the High Court.
The allegation that the acquisition was mala fide or for a collateral purpose had not been pursued before the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to consider those objections for the first time in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal from a decision on a writ petition, the Court was not justified in allowing an objection that had not been raised before the High Court, or an objection the High Court had not been called upon to decide because it was not pursued there.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_decision: The proceeding before the court is an appeal from a decision on a writ petition.
predicates.ground_was_not_raised_or_pursued_before_: The party did not raise the ground below or did not pursue it there.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a writ decision, a ground not raised or pursued below is not considered for the first time on appeal.

issues.legal_issue: The dismissal of a separate civil suit does not restrict relief in an appeal when an appeal from that dismissal remains pending.
material_facts: A separate civil suit seeking a declaration that the acquisition notifications were invalid had been dismissed.
An appeal from the dismissal was pending in the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal of the civil suit did not restrict the Court’s power to issue an appropriate direction in the present appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the separate suit’s dismissal did not restrict its power to grant appropriate relief because an appeal from that dismissal was pending.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The court is deciding an appeal.
predicates.related_civil_suit_was_dismissed: A separate civil suit concerning the same challenged action was dismissed.
predicates.appeal_from_suit_dismissal_is_pending: An appeal from the civil suit’s dismissal remains pending.

issues.definition: When a related civil suit has been dismissed but an appeal from that dismissal is pending, the dismissal does not restrict relief in the current appeal.
